claims: "Ozempic personality" refers to anecdotal reports of emotional blunting, anxiety, depression, or reduced joy (anhedonia) in some users of GLP-1 medications.
Ozempic targets GLP-1 receptors in the brain.
Mood changes associated with "Ozempic personality" are not universal.
"Ozempic personality" is not experienced by all users.
"Ozempic personality" is not a scientifically validated clinical diagnosis.
"Ozempic personality" is a pattern described by users.
"Ozempic personality" is a pattern observed by doctors.
Some users report less interest in sex.
Changes associated with "Ozempic personality" are often temporary.
Some reports indicate that severe depression or suicidal thoughts are associated with GLP-1 drugs.
